subject: Dedicated capacity — EmberTech workload velocity snapshot

From: Priya Shah <priya@embertech.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — EmberTech workload velocity snapshot

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for sending over the template. I pulled together a quick snapshot and attached two files: a short tariff with expected monthly token volumes and a 72-hour sample trace (anonymized). High-level answers below — happy to expand in a follow-up workshop.

- Primary use case: real-time summarization and retrieval-augmented generation inside EmberChat (customer support automation).
- Peak concurrency (concurrent in-flight requests): 420 concurrent sessions for the US region during business hours; baseline trough is ~30.
- Typical prompt length (tokens): 80–160 tokens (multi-turn prompts contain a ~300-token context when we include recent chat history).
- Typical response length (tokens): 40–220 tokens; average ~120 tokens.
- Session persistence: session affinity for 95% of sessions; we prefer KV cache reuse to keep latency low.
- Traffic shape: strong double-peak (09:00–11:00 and 16:00–18:30 PT), expected daily p50 token volume ~1.8M tokens, monthly ~54M tokens. 10% of requests are heavy (long response > 600 tokens).
- SLO: p95 < 250ms for short responses (<120 tokens); p99 budget we need to discuss — current internal goal is < 800ms.
- Preferred model family: open-llm-v2 variants (we're open to quantized 8-bit if accuracy loss is <2% on our eval set).
- Failover: want automatic fallback to a smaller variant if capacity-constrained; prefer no cold starts for active users.

Attachments: embertech_workload_tariff.xlsx (overview), sample_traffic_trace.jsonl (event-level trace).

Let me know what additional clarifying data you need before we do a sizing workshop. We can block 60 minutes next Tue/Thu morning PT.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, EmberTech
priya@embertech.ai

Priya — really helpful, thank you. Quick read-through and a couple clarifying Qs before we schedule the workshop: 

1) For the 420 concurrent sessions peak, is that measured as active token-generation slots (e.g., in-flight GPU attention in same second) or as user sessions with occasional requests? In other words, how bursty are those 420 — sustained vs. short spikes?

2) For the ~10% heavy requests (>600 tokens), are those distributed evenly through the day or concentrated in the late-afternoon peak?

3) You mention 95% session affinity — do you expect affinity to require sticky routing to the same GPU host (stateful) or can you rely on prefix/KV caching with a shared cache layer?

4) Any hard restriction on model quantization (regulatory or accuracy reasons)? You said <2% accuracy loss would be OK — can you point to a single evaluation prompt set we can use to validate candidate quantized builds?

We attached an intake checklist with items that help us produce a first-pass fleet map. If you can drop the Eval set and point-of-contact for SRE during the workshop that would speed things up.

I can put together a quick fleet sketch (nodes by SKU, oversubscription guardrails, and an estimated p95 request latency) after the workshop. Proposed times: Tue Aug 24 at 09:30 PT or Thu Aug 26 at 10:00 PT. Which works?

Thanks —
Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Dylan — good questions, answers inline below: 

1) Measured as concurrent in-flight generations. The 420 number is a 5-minute rolling peak during business hours — about 65% of that is sustained for 2–5 minutes during the morning peak; the rest are short spikes.

2) Heavy requests skew toward the afternoon peak (roughly 2x the morning heavy request proportion).

3) We prefer sticky routing when latency-sensitive (so yes, affinity to keep KV cache warm for VIP customers). For standard users we can tolerate shared caching.

4) No regulatory prohibition on quantization; accuracy-sensitive separation: payments and legal responses must stay on full-precision models. We can provide a 250-sample eval set for accuracy validation (I attached a link in the Drive folder).

We'll take Thu Aug 26 10:00 PT. Ravi (cc) will join from SRE.

—Priya
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Dylan / team — looping in my rough first-pass sizing based on Priya's snapshot and our standard assumptions. Notes and assumptions below; happy to tighten after the workshop and after we ingest the sample trace.

Summary (first-pass):
- Recommended committed pool: 12x A800-equivalent GPUs for primary pool; 3x A800 for warm standby (can be autoscaled for short bursts).
- Expected sustained in-flight slots per A800 (conservative): 40–48 short-response-equivalent concurrent gen slots at 120-token avg output; oversubscribe to 60 for mixed workloads with sticky affinity disabled.
- For 420 concurrent peak (in-flight): 420 / 48 -> ~8.75 => round up to 9 GPUs active. To provide headroom, we propose 12 in pool to keep burst margin and support KV warm cache locality.
- Heavy request handling: route long traces (>600 tokens) to a separate queue backed by the same pool but with conservative batching (batch sizes 1–4) — we budget 3 GPUs headroom to absorb long jobs without impacting short-response p95.
- Latency estimates: p95 short responses (<=120 tokens) on 12x pool: ~180–240ms (depends on kernel selection and quantization). p99 will be higher — separate SLA conversation needed.
- Cost note: committed capacity monthly list-estimate included in the attached stub workbook (embertech_workload_tariff.xlsx) — I filled a placeholder per-GPU monthly rate; finance will refine.

Open clarifying Qs for the workshop:
- Do they require guaranteed p99 SLA for all requests or only for VIP segments?
- Which endpoints require full-precision vs quantized (Priya mentioned payments/legal)?
- How tolerant are they of routing-induced cold cache misses for non-VIP traffic?

Action items:
- Dylan: run the 72-hour trace through our traffic simulator and produce a queueing sketch + suggested autoscale thresholds.
- Ben: finalize SKU mix and oversubscription policy after the workshop; provide 1- and 3-year commitment pricing options.
- Laura: prepare an onboarding runbook and an SLO appendix tailored for sticky-affinity VIP traffic.

Attaching: embertech_workload_tariff.xlsx (first-pass cost worksheet).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
